title: National Consumer Credit Protection Amendment (Small Amount Credit Contract and Consumer Lease Reforms) Bill 2020
short_title: National Consumer Credit Protection Amendment (Small Amount Credit Contract and Consumer Lease Reforms) Bill 2020

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would strengthen protections for people who take out payday loans or rent-to-buy household goods.
It would cap what can be paid under a consumer lease, require equal loan repayments, and stop lenders from charging monthly fees after an early repayment.
It would also cut the protected earnings threshold for payday loans from 20% of gross income to 10% of net income, and apply a similar 10% net income cap to consumer leases.
changes: It would cap total payments under a consumer lease.
It would require equal repayments and equal intervals for small amount credit contracts.
It would remove the ability to charge monthly fees after early repayment.
It would ban marketing of consumer leases at homes.
It would introduce anti-avoidance measures and strengthen penalties.
It would lower the protected earnings threshold for payday loans and introduce one for consumer leases.
summary.affected: Consumers taking out small amount credit contracts (payday loans) and consumer leases (rent-to-buy schemes), as well as the providers of those products.

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The speaker argued for passing the National Consumer Credit Protection Amendment Bill 2020, warning that Afterpay is a "tsunami waiting to happen" with a 90% usage increase and $43 million in late fees, and urged the government to act on predatory payday lending.
